A.4     Rounding error of the full product, Equation (13)
Write xj = s̃j t and assume that exp and expm1 are returned with relative error at most u. Including
the rounding of xj , the computed qj = e−xj has relative error at most (xj + 1)u, and 1 − qj ,
evaluated as − expm1(− fl(xj )), has relative error at most 2u, since xj /(exj − 1) ≤ 1. The exact
coefficients before a convolution step are non-negative and sum to one. Thus the errors in these two
factors contribute at most [(xj + 1)qj + 2(1 − qj )]u to the ℓ1 error. The two multiplications together
contribute at most u, and the addition contributes another u [13, Chapter 3]. To first order, the
error introduced by one convolution step is therefore at most

                         (xj + 1)qj + 2(1 − qj ) + 2 u = 4 + (xj − 1)e−xj u ≤ (4 + e−2 )u.
                                                                                


Convolution with the exact factor, whose ℓ1 norm is one, does not amplify existing errors. Summing
over the n steps gives Equation (13).

B     Error budget details
Table 7 gives the worst absolute error of a placement probability over the extremal set of Section 5.1
as a function of the step and of the field size, and Table 8 the prediction of Equation (11) with κ = 28
for every cell above the rounding floor. The measurements are within a factor 0.70 to 1.09 of the
prediction wherever (n − 1)h ≥ 20, the regime in which the Gaussian bumps dominate. At coarser
steps in small fields, another error scale matters. On a uniform√log t grid, a lone exponential density
                                                                           2
s̃i e−s̃i t has leading aliasing amplitude 2 |Γ(1 + 2πi/h)| ∼ (4π/ h)e−π /h as h → 0, independent of
n: about 5 × 10−8 at h = 1/2 and 2 × 10−16 at 1/4. In a field the density is also multiplied by
coefficients whose factors 1 − e−s̃j t have tails of the same exponential kind, so this figure understates
the error. The measured errors of small fields set the cap at 1/8.

Figure 4: Worst relative error of equities over the extremal set at each size n ≤ 1,000 (solid) as each
window endpoint is varied: xL in the left panel and xR in the right panel. The other endpoint and
the step are fixed at the values of Section 3.3. Dotted colored lines on the left: the same with the

Window. Figure 4 varies the window at the step of Section 3.3. The error stays at the floor while
the endpoints satisfy Proposition 3.1 and rises as soon as they do not: on the left by the amount eStL
the proposition predicts, on the right abruptly, as the window cuts into the density of the smallest
stack. The left condition is the one of the first place; with the first place taken in closed form the
left end can move from −3.75 to −2.75, about 3% of the nodes, and the window is then set by the
second place. On the right the error approximately follows the mass e−s̃min φ(xR −h/2) omitted beyond
xR − h/2, corresponding to an effective end of the trapezoidal sum: 4 × 10−12 at xR = 27.0 for
h = 1/32 and 6 × 10−12 for h = 1/16, within the lattice bound of Section A.1; the floor is reached
at 27.5. The relative error of the last-place probability of a minimal stack that shares the last place
with n − 1 others, which can be n times larger (Section A.1), is 4 × 10−9 at xR = 27.0 for n = 1,000
and reaches its floor at xR = 27.5 as well (not shown).


C     Numerical settings
The settings cover 2 ≤ n ≤ 4,000, the prizes of Section 2.1, and the stack-ratio bound of Equation (4)
with ρ = 109 . Inputs are represented in double precision, with the prizes scaled so that the equities
lie in the normal range of the format. The stacks are sorted and normalized by 20 smax , so that
s̃i ∈ [1/(20ρ), 1/20].
     The grid is the exp-exp lattice t = exp(x − e−x ) with the trapezoidal weights h t (1 + e−x )
on [xL , xR ) = [−3.75, 27.5), with h = 1/8 for 2 ≤ n ≤ 50, 1/16 for 50 < n ≤ 200, 1/32 for
200 < n ≤ 1,000 and 1/64 for 1,000 < n ≤ 4,000 (M = 250, 500, 1,000, 2,000). These fixed ranges
are guided by the error prediction and numerical validation.
     The first place is integrated like the others. The direction rule switches at qi = 1/2, the clamp
interval is [0, C
                cr ] (index shifted by one in the backward direction), and the ahead probabilities are
evaluated as − expm1(−s̃j t).
     The reference implementation used for Section 5 processes the nodes in blocks of 32 (Section 4.3)
and evaluates the blocks in parallel with a fixed assignment of nodes to threads and a fixed order of
reduction.
